name: Patio and outdoor furniture
tagline: Aluminum or rattan frames, bolts that will see rain, and cushions with hidden straps.
peopleNote: Two people. Outdoor sets come in many boxes and the frames are awkward rather than heavy.

tools.why: Many outdoor sets use nuts and bolts rather than threaded inserts.

tools.n: A tube of marine grease or petroleum jelly
tools.why: On the bolt threads. Outdoor hardware seizes with rust and you will want to take this apart one day.

before: Build it on the patio or deck, not in the garage. These sets are wide and often do not fit through a side gate assembled.
Lay a tarp or the cardboard down. Concrete scuffs powder-coated aluminum immediately.
Check the weather. Half-built outdoor furniture left in rain overnight will have rust bloom on the bare bolt ends.
Open every box and group parts by piece — sofa, chairs, table — before building anything. Outdoor sets mix parts across boxes.
safety: Glass table tops are tempered and fail suddenly if an edge is knocked. Two people, handled by the faces.
Never leave a glass-topped patio table without its umbrella hole plug or its umbrella. Wind lifts unsecured tops.

steps.title: Open every box and group by piece
steps.say: Outdoor sets arrive in several boxes and the parts are mixed between them. Open them all and make a pile per piece of furniture before you start.
do: Open all boxes
One pile per chair, one for the sofa, one for the table
Keep each hardware bag with its pile
steps.watch: Building the first chair with the sofa's bolts is extremely easy to do when everything is in one heap.

steps.title: Grease the bolt threads
steps.say: Wipe a little marine grease or petroleum jelly on each bolt thread before it goes in. Two minutes now means these bolts still undo in five years.
do: A dab on the thread of each bolt
Especially any bolt that will sit facing upward and collect water
Wipe excess off the finish
steps.tip: This is the single best piece of outdoor furniture advice. Rusted-solid bolts are why patio sets get thrown away instead of repaired.

steps.title: Build the frames, everything finger-tight
steps.say: Assemble each frame with its bolts, washers and nuts started but loose. Outdoor frames have more flex than indoor ones and need room to find their shape.
do: Washer between bolt head and frame, every time
Nut on the back, finger-tight
All bolts in before any are tightened
steps.watch: Many outdoor bolts need a wrench on the nut while you turn the bolt. Having a second person hold it makes this easy.

steps.title: Check the frames sit flat before tightening
steps.say: Put each frame on a flat surface and press each corner. Adjust while loose until it sits with no rock, then tighten.
do: Each frame on flat ground
Press each corner
Adjust and then tighten, diagonally, two laps
steps.tip: Patios are not level. Get the furniture itself sitting flat on a known-flat surface first, then deal with the patio separately with glides.

steps.title: Fit the feet and glides
steps.say: Push or screw the plastic glides into every leg end. They keep water out of the tube and stop the legs grinding into the patio.
do: One glide per leg, pushed fully in
Adjustable feet: leave room to adjust
Check none are missing
steps.watch: An open aluminum leg end fills with water, and in winter that water freezes and splits the tube. Every leg needs its cap.

steps.title: Fit the table top
steps.say: Slat tops screw down from underneath. Glass tops sit on rubber pads and clamp gently. Two people either way.
do: Slat top: screws from underneath, started loose then tightened in a cross pattern
Glass top: clean rubber pads first, then lower it straight down
Clamps on glass: finger-tight plus a nudge, no more
steps.watch: Over-tightening a clamp on a tempered glass top is a classic way to shatter it, sometimes days later rather than immediately.

steps.title: Umbrella hole and plug
steps.say: If there is an umbrella hole, fit the plug now or put the umbrella in. An open hole in a glass top is a stress point and a wind catcher.
do: Plug in if no umbrella
Umbrella through the hole and into the base, if using
Never use an umbrella without a weighted base
steps.tip: A patio umbrella in a table with no weighted base will lift in a gust and take the glass with it.

steps.title: Strap the cushions on
steps.say: Most outdoor cushions have velcro strips or ties underneath. Use them. Unsecured cushions end up in the neighbor's garden.
do: Find the velcro or ties on the cushion underside
Fasten them around the frame rails
Seat cushions first, then backs
steps.tip: If there are no straps, a few outdoor velcro strips from a hardware store solve it for a couple of dollars.

steps.title: Final tighten and a wobble check
steps.say: Second tightening lap on every piece, then sit in each seat and rock. Any movement is a loose bolt.
do: Full second lap on every piece
Sit and rock in each seat
Check the table does not rack when leaned on
steps.tip: Keep the Allen key and a small wrench in a drawer. Outdoor furniture expands and contracts with temperature and needs a tighten each spring.

steps.title: Plan for weather from day one
steps.say: Bring cushions in or get a cover. Sun fades fabric faster than anything, and water in the frame is what eventually kills these sets.
do: Cushion storage bag or bring them inside
A fitted cover for the frames if they stay out all winter
Tip tables up or cover them so water drains
steps.tip: Set a spring reminder: tighten every bolt, check every glide, re-grease anything that looks rusty. That is a twenty-year patio set instead of a three-year one.

fixes.a: Replace it with a stainless steel bolt of the same size from a hardware store, and grease the thread. Unlike bunk beds, outdoor furniture bolts are usually generic and safe to substitute like for like.

fixes.q: The chair rocks on my patio
fixes.a: Check the frame itself on flat ground first. If the frame is fine, the patio is uneven — use adjustable glides or a thin shim under the short leg.

fixes.q: The glass top will not sit flat
fixes.a: A rubber pad is missing or out of position, or there is grit on one. Lift the glass with two people, clean everything, reposition the pads, lower straight down.

fixes.q: A bolt is seized and will not undo
fixes.a: Penetrating oil, left overnight, then try again. If the head is rounded off, a bolt extractor or a hacksaw cut is the next step. Grease on assembly prevents all of this.
Use the straps underneath. If the cushions have none, outdoor velcro strips or a few cushion clips solve it permanently.

fixes.q: A leg filled with water and split
fixes.a: The glide cap was missing. Replace the glide, and check every other leg. Aluminum splits when water inside freezes, and that damage is not repairable.
